cleanIntro: This guide comes from Browning's own owner's manual for the Auto-5 Magnum, the 3-inch 12 and 20 gauge long-recoil autoloader. The barrel itself recoils on this gun: it rides back along the magazine tube against a big recoil spring and a stack of friction rings, so the magazine tube and those rings are the heart of the cleaning. The field strip is the barrel off the front of the gun, nothing more. Browning says plainly not to take the action apart, and its book ends there. The Light 12 and Light 20 Auto-5 have a different recoil setup and their own book, so nothing here about friction rings applies to them.

steps.title: Safety on: push the button to the right
steps.action: Point the muzzle somewhere safe and keep your fingers away from the trigger. The safety is the cross bolt at the rear of the trigger guard. Push it to the right to put the gun on safe; pushed left, a red band shows and the gun can fire. A competent gunsmith can reverse it for a left-hander, so check which way yours is installed before you trust the directions.
steps.quote: To place the gun "ON SAFE," press the "safety" button to the right.
steps.cite: Browning Auto 5 Magnum Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Operation of the "Safety"
steps.warn: DO NOT DEPEND ON THE RED COLOR ALONE TO INDICATE YOUR GUN'S SAFETY STATUS.

steps.title: Cut-off lever forward, so the magazine can empty
steps.action: Look at the magazine cut-off, the lever at the front of the left side of the receiver. Pulled back, it locks shells in the magazine tube so they will not feed. That is useful for swapping a load in the field, but it means cycling the action will not empty the tube. Push the lever forward before you unload so every shell in the magazine can come out.
steps.quote: Push the cut-off lever forward when you desire to release the shells in the magazine so that they will feed
steps.cite: Browning Auto 5 Magnum Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Operation of the Magazine Cut-off

steps.title: Cycle the operating handle until nothing comes out
steps.action: With the safety on and the muzzle pointed safely, grasp the operating handle on the right side of the receiver and cycle the action, again and again, until no more shells are ejected. This is the way Browning recommends unloading the Auto-5. Count the shells as they come out against what you loaded, and put them away from the bench.
steps.quote: The recommended way to unload the Auto-5 is simply to grasp the operating handle and cycle the action until all rounds are ejected.
steps.cite: Browning Auto 5 Magnum Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Unloading > Unloading your Auto-5

steps.title: Look into the chamber, the carrier and the magazine tube
steps.action: Do not take the empty ejections as proof. Look into the chamber, check the carrier underneath, and look and feel into the magazine tube to be sure there are no shells left anywhere. Browning repeats that an open breech after shooting is not an unloaded gun. Keep all ammunition away from where you will clean.
steps.quote: ALWAYS INSPECT THE CHAMBER, CARRIER AND MAGAZINE TUBE TO BE SURE THEY CONTAIN NO CARTRIDGES.
steps.cite: Browning Auto 5 Magnum Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Unloading > Breech Remains Open After the Last Shot
steps.warn: EVEN WITH THE BREECH OPEN AFTER SHOOTING, DO NOT ASSUME YOUR SHOTGUN IS UNLOADED.

steps.title: Breech bolt back and locked open
steps.action: Draw the breech bolt all the way back with the operating handle until it locks open, and leave the safety on. Put on safety glasses: Browning asks for them during all disassembly and cleaning, because the recoil spring around the magazine tube is strong. The bolt stays locked back for the whole strip.
steps.quote: Draw the breech bolt rearward and lock it open.
steps.cite: Browning Auto 5 Magnum Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Disassembly Procedures, step 1

steps.title: Hold the barrel back, unscrew the cap, forearm off
steps.action: Rest the butt of the stock on a firm surface, muzzle up. With your left hand, press the barrel rearward and keep that pressure on, because the recoil spring is pushing it forward. With your right hand, unscrew the magazine cap, then slide the wooden forearm forward off the magazine tube. Do not squeeze the open rear end of the forearm hard, or the wood can split.
steps.quote: With the left hand apply rearward pressure to the barrel, then unscrew the magazine cap with the right hand.
steps.cite: Browning Auto 5 Magnum Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Disassembly Procedures, step 2
steps.warn: DO NOT SQUEEZE HARD ON THE OPEN REAR END OF THE FOREARM. TOO MUCH PRESSURE COULD CAUSE THE WOOD TO SPLIT.

steps.title: Let the barrel forward slowly and slide it off
steps.action: Keep a firm hold on the barrel and ease the pressure off gradually, letting the recoil spring push it forward under your control. Then slide the barrel straight forward off the magazine tube. If you let go all at once, the spring can throw the barrel off the gun. The recoil spring, friction rings and friction brakes stay on the magazine tube.
steps.quote: While continuing to hold the barrel firmly, gradually release pressure and slide the barrel directly forward off the magazine tube.
steps.cite: Browning Auto 5 Magnum Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Disassembly Procedures, step 3
steps.warn: DO NOT SUDDENLY RELEASE PRESSURE AGAINST THE BARREL.

steps.title: Leave the bolt open while the barrel is off
steps.action: With the barrel out, the breech bolt stays locked back. Do not press the bolt release button. With no barrel extension to stop it, the bolt would run forward and the operating handle would hit the front edge of the ejection port and damage the receiver. If you ever must close it with the barrel off, hold the operating handle while you press the release and let the bolt ride home slowly.
steps.quote: AFTER THE BARREL HAS BEEN REMOVED FROM YOUR GUN, LEAVE THE BREECH BOLT IN THE OPEN POSITION. DO NOT PRESS THE BOLT RELEASE BUTTON.
steps.cite: Browning Auto 5 Magnum Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Disassembly Procedures, step 4

no.q: AFTER THE BARREL HAS BEEN REMOVED FROM YOUR GUN, LEAVE THE BREECH BOLT IN THE OPEN POSITION. DO NOT PRESS THE BOLT RELEASE BUTTON.
no.src: Browning Auto 5 Magnum Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Disassembly Procedures, step 4

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: On the bench now: the barrel, the forearm, the magazine cap, and the action with the stock, still carrying the recoil spring and friction rings on its magazine tube. Browning's cleaning starts exactly here, with the barrel off so it can be cleaned from the breech end. This is as far apart as the book takes the gun.
steps.quote: Remove the barrel so that it can be cleaned from the breech end.
steps.cite: Browning Auto 5 Magnum Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Cleaning and Maintenance Suggestions > CLEANING YOUR AUTO-5, step 1

steps.title: Rod and patch in from the breech end
steps.action: Use a shotgun cleaning rod with a tip and a patch big enough to fit the bore snugly. Put it in at the breech end and run it back and forth through the bore several times. Then look through the bore from both ends toward a light for leading, which shows as dull streaks along the bore, usually near the muzzle and just ahead of the chamber.
steps.quote: insert the rod and patch in the breech end of the barrel and run back and forth through the the bore several times.
steps.cite: Browning Auto 5 Magnum Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Cleaning and Maintenance Suggestions > CLEANING YOUR AUTO-5, step 2

steps.title: Heavy leading: brass brush and solvent, all the way through
steps.action: Some leading is normal and not serious. If it gets heavy, make sure a choke tube is fitted, spray the bore or a brass bore brush with powder solvent, and scrub until it is gone. Push the brush all the way out of the bore before you pull it back, so bristles do not break off. Finish with a clean dry patch, then a lightly oiled one.
steps.quote: To prevent brass bristles from breaking off, the brush should be pushed completely through the bore before being withdrawn.
steps.cite: Browning Auto 5 Magnum Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Cleaning and Maintenance Suggestions > CLEANING YOUR AUTO-5, steps 4-5

steps.title: Choke tube out, threads wiped and oiled
steps.action: If your barrel is threaded for Invector-Plus tubes, take the tube out with the Invector wrench: turn it counterclockwise to break it loose, then finger twist it the rest of the way out. Wipe the tube, its threads and the barrel threads, and oil them lightly. Older Auto-5 barrels and the Buck Special are fixed-choke; skip this if yours has no tube.
steps.quote: Use the Invector wrench to loosen the tube, turning it counterclockwise.
steps.cite: Browning Auto 5 Magnum Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — lnvector Interchangeable Choke System > TUBE REMOVAL, step 3
steps.warn: DO NOT FIRE THIS SHOTGUN WITHOUT HAVING AN INVECTOR CHOKE TUBE INSTALLED.

steps.title: Magazine tube wiped clean and lightly oiled
steps.action: The barrel rides on the magazine tube every shot, so this tube matters more than on most shotguns. Wipe all the dirt and grit off it, then oil it lightly with an oiled patch. Use a good oil that stays fluid in the cold: oil that thickens or goes gummy slows the barrel and the gun can fail to eject. More oil on the tube means more recoil to the action, which can help a light load eject.
steps.quote: The magazine tube on the Automatic-5 should be wiped clean of all dirt and grit, and then lubricated lightly with an oiled patch.
steps.cite: Browning Auto 5 Magnum Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Cleaning and Maintenance Suggestions > CLEANING YOUR AUTO-5, step 7

steps.title: Friction rings set for the shells you will shoot
steps.action: The friction pieces go back in the arrangement for your loads. For 3-inch magnums, with the butt down: a ring on the spring beveled side up, a brake, a ring beveled side down, a ring beveled side up, then the second brake. For 2 3/4-inch magnum, high-velocity and all steel shot loads, the top two rings and brake come off entirely, not tucked under the spring. Keep the removed parts somewhere safe, and if the setting is wrong the gun will pound itself.
steps.quote: This is the correct position for all 3-inch magnum loads.
steps.cite: Browning Auto 5 Magnum Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Friction Ring Adjustment for Auto-5 3-inch Magnum Models, step 3
steps.warn: THE FOLLOWING INSTRUCTIONS ARE ONLY FOR 3-INCH 12 AND 20-GAUGE MODELS, NOT FOR THE 2 3/4" LIGHT 12 GAUGE OR 2 3/4" LIGHT 20 GAUGE AUTOMATIC.

steps.title: Never take off the bronze friction piece
steps.action: Behind the barrel guide ring sits a bronze friction piece. It stays where it is. Browning says never to remove it under any circumstances: without it the friction ring or recoil spring bears directly on the barrel guide ring, deforms it, and lets through so much recoil that the mechanism is pounded severely. Clean and oil around it in place.
steps.quote: NEVER UNDER ANY CIRCUMSTANCES REMOVE THE BRONZE FRICTION PIECE FROM ITS POSITION REARWARD OF THE BARREL GUIDE RING.
steps.cite: Browning Auto 5 Magnum Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Schematics and Parts List

no.q: NEVER UNDER ANY CIRCUMSTANCES REMOVE THE BRONZE FRICTION PIECE FROM ITS POSITION REARWARD OF THE BARREL GUIDE RING.
no.src: Browning Auto 5 Magnum Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Schematics and Parts List

steps.title: A drop on each receiver track, and no more
steps.action: Now and then put a small drop of oil on each track inside the receiver where the breech bolt and the barrel extension guides run. After weather or handling, give the metal parts a light film of oil. Do not pour oil into the action: the excess runs back into the stock wood, softens it and loosens the stock.
steps.quote: DO NOT POUR LARGE QUANTITIES OF OIL INTO THE ACTION.
steps.cite: Browning Auto 5 Magnum Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Cleaning and Maintenance Suggestions > PERIODIC OILING

steps.title: Do not take the action apart
steps.action: The action is not stripped for cleaning. Browning calls it a specialized, finely fitted mechanism that can be marred for life by an attempt to remove the inner parts, and says it is unnecessary for routine cleaning and oiling. If the gun has been dropped in water or met some other misfortune, Browning recommends taking it straight to a competent gunsmith.
steps.quote: DO NOT TAKE YOUR GUN'S ACTION APART.
steps.cite: Browning Auto 5 Magnum Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Cleaning and Maintenance Suggestions

no.q: DO NOT TAKE YOUR GUN'S ACTION APART.
no.src: Browning Auto 5 Magnum Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Cleaning and Maintenance Suggestions

steps.title: Oiled cloth on the metal, oil or wax on the wood
steps.action: With the barrel back on, wipe all the exposed metal with an oiled cloth, getting every finger mark, because moisture collects there. Check the barrel and action for any cleaning patch left behind. The wood can be wiped with gun oil or polished with a good furniture wax, but use one or the other, not both.
steps.quote: The wood surfaces can also be wiped with Browning Oil or they can be polished with any quality furniture wax (but not both).
steps.cite: Browning Auto 5 Magnum Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Cleaning and Maintenance Suggestions > CLEANING YOUR AUTO-5, step 10

deepAbsentReason: Browning's Auto-5 Magnum book ends at the barrel-off field strip and forbids going further: under Cleaning and Maintenance Suggestions it says "DO NOT TAKE YOUR GUN'S ACTION APART." and sends a gun that needs more, such as one dropped in water, to a competent gunsmith. There is no deeper procedure to follow.

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: Barrel off, and the rod goes in from the breech end
A patch big enough to fit snugly, run back and forth several times
Look through from both ends toward a light for leading streaks, usually near the muzzle and just ahead of the chamber
Heavy leading: choke tube fitted, powder solvent, brass brush pushed all the way through before it comes back
Clean dry patch, then a lightly oiled patch
Check that no patch is left in the barrel or the action

cleaning.name: INVECTOR CHOKE TUBE
tasks: Tube out with the Invector wrench, counterclockwise, then by hand
Tube, tube threads and barrel threads wiped and lightly oiled
Tube back in by hand, tapered end first, then firmly seated with the wrench
Do not fire the gun without a choke tube in a threaded barrel
Invector-Plus and standard Invector tubes are not interchangeable

cleaning.name: MAGAZINE TUBE & FRICTION RINGS
tasks: Magazine tube wiped clean of dirt and grit, then oiled lightly with an oiled patch
A good oil that stays fluid in the cold; gummy oil can stop the gun ejecting
Friction rings and brakes set for the loads you will shoot
Never remove the bronze friction piece behind the barrel guide ring

cleaning.name: RECEIVER & ACTION
tasks: A small drop of oil now and then on each receiver track
Light film of oil on the metal after weather or handling
Do not pour oil into the action; it runs into the stock wood
Do not take the action apart

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR & WOOD
tasks: All exposed metal wiped with an oiled cloth, finger marks included
Wood: gun oil or furniture wax, not both

reassembly: Make sure the chamber, carrier and magazine are empty, and the breech bolt is locked back.
Check the friction rings and brakes on the magazine tube are set for the loads you will shoot.

Rest the butt on a firm surface. Put the barrel guide ring around the magazine tube and push the barrel back against the recoil spring, guiding the barrel extension into the receiver with its guides in the receiver tracks.
Keep rearward pressure on the barrel so the front of the barrel extension is even with or just inside the front of the receiver.
Slide the forearm back over the magazine tube without squeezing its rear end, and screw the magazine cap on tightly.
Be sure the cap is all the way down, pressing the rear of the forearm firmly against the receiver, with the wood ridge at the back of the forearm in the groove at the front of the receiver.
fncheck: With the gun empty and pointed somewhere safe, check the magazine cap is screwed all the way down and the forearm is tight against the receiver. With the barrel on, press the bolt release and let the bolt close; it stops against the barrel extension. Pull the operating handle back and check the bolt locks open again. Move the safety to the right and to the left and feel it move positively both ways, with the red band showing only when it is off safe; do not snap the firing pin on an empty chamber to test it. Push the magazine cut-off lever back and forward and feel it move both ways. If your barrel takes a choke tube, check it is in and tight. Never test the gun's function with live ammunition.
